selected.title: The Assessment Audit
selected.audienceGap: Students assume a degree's name reveals the assessment style.
selected.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
selected.viewerChange: Learns to ask about assessment criteria rather than guessing based on degree titles.
selected.concept: A student compares two sample tasks side-by-side using a three-column audit sheet.
selected.device: Split-screen comparison of a task, an assessment criterion, and a feedback source.
selected.support: The method separates three different pieces of information; it does not assume particular course content.
methodSteps: Ask what criterion is used to assess it.
Ask what feedback is available; mark unknown answers as questions.
selected.interpretationRule: Use the unanswered cells to ask a precise question about the actual course or task before deciding.
selected.visibleProof: A three-column question sheet turns one vague preference into a concrete unanswered question.
selected.payoff: The student identifies a specific missing piece of information for their inquiry.
selected.limitations: This is a question-forming aid, not a degree ranking, aptitude test or prediction of success.

demonstration.input: Two sample tasks: a financial reconciliation and a marketing plan.
demonstration.visibleInput: Example: Task: Analyze variance. Assessment: Rubric or Answer Key?
demonstration.observation: The student realizes the task is clear, but the grading criteria remains unknown.
demonstration.nextQuestion: What specific rubric criteria is used to grade this?

comparedWith.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
comparedWith.device: Split-screen comparison of a task, an assessment criterion, and a feedback source.

comparedWith.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
comparedWith.device: A personal notebook entry showing the transition from 'I'm stuck' to 'I need this answer'.

comparedWith.hlni: One unlabeled example does not prove which category or programme contains it. An exclusive claim needs information that actually links the example to that category.
comparedWith.device: A 'reveal' animation showing the lack of institutional source for the example.

conceptSelection.contrast: Pre-story comparison selected different grounded insights and mechanisms: Trust = assessment_questions / audit_worksheet; Connection = task_question_journal / journal_method; Discovery = insufficient_information / evidence_gap. Each has an illustrative input, observable result and next question. This is not editorial approval.

hlni.insight: A task label alone does not reveal what is assessed; assessment criteria are distinct from task descriptions.
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume the degree name or subject title implies the method of evaluation and feedback.
hlni.viewerChange: The viewer moves from guessing based on labels to asking for specific assessment rubrics.
hlni.support: Separating 'Task' from 'Assessment' forces an investigation into grading standards rather than relying on assumed difficulty or relevance.
hlni.payoff: The student identifies that the 'variance' task is insufficient information, leading to a precise question about the grading rubric.

reelTitle: The Assessment Audit: B.Com vs BBA
creativeAngle: Moving from vague degree titles to concrete assessment evaluation
objective: Enable students to evaluate course content objectively using a structured assessment audit
targetAudience: +2 students seeking academic depth and well-supported course and career decisions

shots.name: The Title Trap
shots.visual: Student looking confused at two brochures labelled B.Com and BBA.
shots.dialogue: Choosing between B.Com and BBA by title is a guess.

shots.name: The Vague Assumption
shots.visual: Student holding a pen, staring at a blank notebook.
shots.dialogue: The name rarely reveals how you are actually tested.
shots.cameraPerformance: Medium shot, panning to the desk.

shots.name: The Audit Sheet Reveal
shots.visual: Student places a three-column audit sheet on the desk.
shots.dialogue: Try this audit. Map the tasks against the criteria.

shots.name: The Task Comparison
shots.visual: Close up on the sheet showing: Task: Analyze variance. Assessment: Rubric or Answer Key?
shots.dialogue: Task: Analyze variance. Assessment: Rubric or Answer Key? You see the task, but the grading criteria is missing.
shots.onscreenText: Example: Task: Analyze variance. Assessment: Rubric or Answer Key?
shots.cameraPerformance: Tight focus on the paper worksheet.

shots.name: The Specific Inquiry
shots.visual: Student circles the missing criterion on the sheet.
shots.dialogue: Now you have a concrete question: What rubric criteria is used?
shots.onscreenText: Ask: What specific rubric criteria is used to grade this?

shots.name: Actionable Next Step
shots.visual: Student looks up from the sheet, ready to visit a faculty office.
shots.dialogue: Use this audit to ask precise questions before deciding.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Shifting the focus from degree labels to assessment criteria using a three-column audit method.
